flawed_step: Line 0024: "It suffices to show that $\chi(\partial G)=3$ in order to establish that $G$ is 3-colourable" (used together with the cited fact $\chi(\overline{G})=3$); the whole argument of line 0026 rests on this sufficiency claim.
counterexample: The sufficiency claim is a non-sequitur: a graph split into an 'interior' part and a 'boundary' part can have both parts 3-colourable while the whole graph is not. Explicit counterexample: the 5-wheel W5 with vertices h, v1, v2, v3, v4, v5 and edges v1v2, v2v3, v3v4, v4v5, v5v1 (the 'boundary' cycle) together with hv1, hv2, hv3, hv4, hv5. The 'boundary' part induced on {v1,...,v5} is C5 with chi = 3 (colour v1=1, v2=2, v3=1, v4=2, v5=3). The 'interior' part induced on {h} is K1 with chi = 1 <= 3. Yet chi(W5) = 4: any proper colouring of the odd cycle C5 must use 3 colours on v1..v5, and h is adjacent to all of them, so h needs a 4th colour. So knowing each of the two parts is 3-colourable gives no bound on the whole graph, because the two colourings need not be compatible across the edges joining them. In the proof's setting the arcs joining boundary vertices to interior intersection points are exactly the edges the argument ignores. Separately, the quantity the proof tries to bound is vacuous: partial-G is by the proof's own definition (line 0021) a cycle of length 2n, an even cycle, so chi(partial G) = 2 unconditionally; the elaborate G+x / 4-colour-theorem argument of line 0026 therefore establishes nothing that was not already trivial, and cannot bridge to chi(G) = 3.
reasoning_summary: The proof's engine is the claim (line 0024) that chi(G-bar) = 3 plus chi(boundary G) = 3 implies chi(G) = 3. This inference is invalid because proper colourings of two vertex-disjoint parts need not extend to a proper colouring of the union: the edges between the parts are unconstrained by the two separate facts. W5 = C5 + hub is a concrete refutation with the same shape (3-chromatic boundary cycle, 1-chromatic interior, 4-chromatic whole). The failure is compounded because the boundary of G is an even (2n) cycle, hence 2-colourable outright, so line 0026's G+x argument bounds something already trivial. The author's own UPDATE at line 0001 concedes the same gap. Since the sole engine of the deduction fails, the proof does not establish chi(G) = 3.
notes: Counterexample is to the proof's key inference step, not to the theorem statement itself (which may well be true).
